excerpt: Muzz, formerly Muzmatch, is a London Muslim marriage and dating app founded by Shahzad Younas. Free to match and chat, with a paid Gold upgrade.
content:
Muzz (formerly Muzmatch) is a dating and marriage app for Muslims. Members create profiles, swipe and match, chat, and can make video and voice calls without sharing their phone number, with privacy options such as blurring photos until there is a match (as TechCrunch described in 2017) and including a chaperone, or wali, in conversations. Its website says it is always free to see profiles, match, chat and marry on Muzz, and it sells a paid Gold membership with extra features. It also runs events and has launched Muzz Social, a social network for Muslims.

Shahzad Younas founded the app and runs it as CEO; the company is headquartered in London. UKTN reported in 2024 that Muzz was the first Muslim-focused startup backed by Y Combinator, had raised more than $9 million from investors including FJ Labs and Luxor Capital, and said it had 10 million members and that more than half a million people had married after meeting on it. TechCrunch covered Muzmatch's YC debut in 2017 and a $7 million Series A in 2019. The app has since rebranded as Muzz; its homepage now claims 20 million Muslim members and more than a million success stories, figures that are the company's own.

Muzz is free to download and use for the core features. Muzz Gold, the paid tier, costs money and is priced in the app by country and subscription length; we did not find a public price list.

We have not used Muzz for this page. It brings together Muzz's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
